title: Accordion
description: Lets you show and hide content, on its own or as a group.

title: Anchor
description: A structural primitive to enable CSS Anchor Positioning on stuff.

title: Avatar
description: Avatars show a person or entity as an image, initials or icon.

title: Badge
description: Badges attach a small count or status dot to another element.

title: Button group
description: Groups related buttons.

title: Button
description: Buttons allow users to take actions, and make choices, with a single tap.

title: Callout
description: Callouts call out for user attention. Should be part of the flow and used without interrupting the user's task.
keywords: alert banner message box notice warning

title: Card
description:
The card is extremely versatile and can be used on its own, or as a building
    block for accordions, dialogs and more.

title: Carousel
description: A scrolling list with snap points, buttons and markers.

title: Checkbox
description:
Use a Checkbox for choices that are submitted with a form. For a setting
    that applies right away, use a Switch, and for options in a toolbar a Toggle. See also: Checkbox field group.

title: Chip
description:
Chips are compact elements that represent an input, attribute, or action.
    Use them for filters, tags and choices. For the main action, like Save or
    Send, use a Button.

title: Copy
description: A button that copies text or a field's value to the clipboard.

title: Description list
description: Description lists are used to display a list of terms and their descriptions.

title: Dialog
description: A minimally styled window overlaid on the main content. By design the Dialog is minimal with zero content to allow for both modal and non-modal use.

title: Divider
description: It's just a line.

title: Drawer
description:
Slides in from the sides, top or bottom of the screen. Good for navigation,
    filters and side content. For a question or a short task that needs the
    user's full attention, use a Dialog.

title: Form
description: Spacing and grouping for form fields.

title: Layout
description:
Six classes for the space between components: .ui-layout-column,
    .ui-layout-row, .ui-layout-grid, .ui-layout-columns, .ui-layout-media and .ui-layout-container. Put
    them on wrapper elements, such as div, section or
    ul. They sit in the utils layer, so on a component they
    replace its own layout. Their gaps come from the --ui-space-* scale, so they follow --ui-space-scale.

title: List
description: Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text and images and video. Use lists to help users find a specific item and act on it.

title: Menu
description: A popover list of actions or links.

title: Message
description: Chat bubbles that group by sender, with attachments, reactions and a typing indicator.

title: Number field
description: A number field with buttons that step the value down and up, for amounts like a quantity.

title: One-time code
description: A one-time password (OTP) field: one input drawn as a box per character, with paste and SMS autofill.

title: Progress
description: See also: Spinner.

title: Radio
description: See also: Form documentation.

title: Range
description: Range lets users pick a number by sliding a thumb along a track.

title: Rating
description: A star rating: a meter that shows a score, or radios that collect one.

title: Select
description:
Leverages the List component to provide markup for the Select popover. Use a Select to pick a value in a
    form. For actions, use a Menu.

title: Spinner
description:
Add it to an element with aria-busy="true". Spinners are always
    indeterminate. See also: Progress bar.

title: 1. Because it's blocked by another use case
Stat
description: A stat shows one number with its label and the change behind it.

title: Stepper
description: Shows where someone is in a flow of steps, such as a checkout.

title: Switch
description: Use a Switch for a setting that applies right away. Use a Checkbox for choices that are submitted with a form, and a Toggle for options in a toolbar. See also: Switch field group.

title: Table
description: Displays tabular data. Basic tables with row and column headers, and optional captions and footers.

title: Tabs
description:
The Tabs are radio inputs and the Panels are just divs that show and hide
    based on the radio inputs' :checked state. Use Tabs to switch between
    panels of content. To pick an option, like a list or grid view, use a Toggle group.

title: Text field
description: An input for single-line text data. Basic text fields with labels, field descriptions, and validation states.
keywords: email input password search text box

title: Textarea
description: An input for multi-line text data. Basic textareas with labels, supporting text, and validation states.

title: Timeline
description: A list of dated events with markers and a connecting line.

title: Toast
description: Short messages that confirm an action and dismiss themselves.

title: Toggle
description: Toggle buttons and toggle groups switch options on and off, alone or as a set.

title: Tooltip
description:
Built on top of Anchor.
    
    
      
        Wrap the trigger in <Tooltip> and pass a stable{" "}
        id. Set interestfor with that id on the trigger
        element itself (it only works on real invokers like{" "}
        <button> or <a>). Put the tooltip
        in
        TooltipContent after the trigger.

title: Typography
description:
Styles for headings, body text, and other text content. Use util classes
    anywhere or wrap content in .ui-rich-text.

title: Accessibility
description:
A few basics to get you started. OPUI leans on native HTML, so a lot comes
    for free, but you still decide the names, the order and the content. Test
    with a keyboard and a screen reader, it always depends.

title: Acknowledgments
description:
Open Props UI stands on a lot of shoulders. These are the people, projects
    and resources that made it possible.

title: Browser support
description:
The web platform features the components rely on, and the browsers that ship
    each one.

title: Concepts
description:
The architecture: cascade layers, token tiers, scopes, props and classes,
    naming, rich text, and where JavaScript is still needed.

title: Customizing
description:
Where your CSS goes: a theme in theme.custom changes the whole library,
    a component's --_* properties change one component or one instance,
    and your own layer holds the rest.

title: Migrating from v5 to v6
description:
The breaking changes in v6 and how to update your code, component by
    component.

title: Theme tokens
description:
Every token theme.css and core/palette.css declare,
    with its default and its tier, and the instance inputs components read. Most are roles; the others are
    marked knob, primitive, hook, component
    or input. The tests check every promised contrast ratio in light
    and dark mode, with and without more contrast.

title: Theming
description:
The knobs and roles behind colors, density, spacing, corners, fonts,
    elevation, motion and contrast, and the classes that scope them.

title: Why Open Props UI?
description:
Components built from the HTML and CSS the platform ships today, as files
    you can read, copy and own.

title: Getting started
description:
Add the CSS from the CDN, from npm or by copying the files, then write the
    class names.

title: An accordion that animates to auto
description: interpolate-size and ::details-content let a details element transition to its natural height.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interpolate-size JavaScript that measures the content and animates a pixel height. `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` and `::details-content` transition a `<details>` to its natural height. details-content interpolate-size

title: Hover cards without JavaScript
description: interestfor, popover=hint and anchor positioning open a hover card on hover and focus.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interestfor Timers for hover intent, focus and blur listeners, and a positioning library that measures and flips the card. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning places it. anchor-positioning interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Squircle avatars with corner-shape
description: aspect-ratio, :has(img) and corner-shape for avatars.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback corner-shape An SVG mask or a `clip-path` path: a fixed shape that clips borders and shadows too. `corner-shape: squircle` draws the corner, and `aspect-ratio: 1` keeps the avatar square. aspect-ratio corner-shape has

title: One Button, no IconButton
description: :has(> svg:only-child) turns any Button into an icon button.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback Gotchas :has() A separate `IconButton` component or an `iconOnly` prop, with every size and variant built twice. `:has(> svg:only-child)` lets the button see that it only holds an icon. has

title: Severity colors from one source color
description: Relative colors and light-dark() derive every severity shade from one color.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback oklch(from …) 40 hand-picked colors for five severities in two schemes, or a preprocessor that only works at build time. One `--ui-palette-source` per severity, and `oklch(from …)` derives every shade. light-dark relative-color

title: A carousel made of CSS
description: Scroll snap, ::scroll-button() and ::scroll-marker: a carousel without JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback ::scroll-button() JavaScript that listens to scroll events to run the buttons and dots, with their accessibility done by hand. `::scroll-button()` and `::scroll-marker` generate focusable buttons and dots. scroll-buttons scroll-markers scroll-snap

title: Drawing a checkbox
description: appearance: none, a clip-path checkmark and system colors for a native checkbox.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A hidden input and a fake box with an SVG check that mirrors every state. `appearance: none` lets the real input draw its own box and check. appearance clip-path

title: Leader lines with grid
description: A container query and a grid pseudo-element draw dotted leader lines.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @container A row of clipped dots, a repeating background or an empty filler element, and a media query that only knows the viewport. A grid per pair with a dotted `::after` between term and description, and a container query for the column. container-queries

title: Dialogs without JavaScript
description: Invoker commands, closedby and @starting-style for modal dialogs.
headings: The problem The trick Keyboard shortcuts Try it Scroll lock Fallback closedby A click handler for `showModal()`, another for `close()`, and a backdrop listener that checks where the click landed. `commandfor`, `command` and `closedby` open and close it, `@starting-style` fades it in, and `allow-discrete` fades it out. dialog-closedby invoker-commands overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Sliding drawers with @starting-style
description: A dialog that slides in from any edge, and out again with allow-discrete.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @starting-style A fixed `<div>` with JavaScript for the focus trap, Esc and backdrop clicks, and a class removed after `transitionend` to animate it out. A modal `<dialog>` that slides with `translate`, `@starting-style` and `allow-discrete`. overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Fluid type with progress()
description: progress() turns the viewport width into one 0 to 1 ramp that every heading size shares.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback progress() A clamp() per heading with a hand-tuned vi slope, so every heading grew over a different range of viewport widths. `progress(100vi, start, end)` is one shared ramp, and each heading mixes its two steps with it. progress-function

title: Smarter fieldsets with :has()
description: :has() lets fieldsets and legends style themselves from what they contain.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :has(:required) Modifier classes or props kept in sync with what the fieldset contains. `:has()` lets the fieldset and legend style themselves from their content. has

title: Menus with popover and anchor positioning
description: Popover, invoker commands and anchor positioning: a menu with no JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback popover JavaScript to toggle and dismiss it, `z-index` fights, and a positioning library that measures and flips. `popover`, invoker commands and anchor positioning, with the trigger as the implicit anchor. anchor-positioning invoker-commands popover

title: Styling the native progress bar
description: appearance: none and :indeterminate on the native progress element.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :indeterminate A `<div role="progressbar">` with its ARIA attributes kept in sync by hand. The native `<progress>` with `appearance: none`, so the role and the value stay native. appearance container-style-queries indeterminate

title: Range sliders with datalist ticks
description: A scroll-driven gradient fill and datalist tick marks for input range.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback <datalist> Vendor pseudo-elements, a fill only Firefox could draw, and tick labels that never showed. A scroll-driven animation on the thumb fills the track, and `display: flex` brings the `<datalist>` labels back. datalist input-range scroll-driven-animations

title: opui 6.0
description: What changed in 6.0 and why, with live demos.
headings: It's a proper design system now Four example themes Token tiers Contrast as a guarantee Loads of new components So much cool stuff in the docs Blocks! Theme builder The CSS is the component Slots become parts, props get one naming model The platform did the work Browser support, honestly The new "by hand" Where it landed Migrating

title: A select you can style
description: appearance: base-select, ::picker(select) and :open for a fully styled select.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback base-select A rebuilt listbox: a button, a popup, ARIA roles and JavaScript for focus, keyboard and typeahead. `appearance: base-select` makes the real `<select>` stylable, with `<selectedcontent>` and `::picker(select)`. customizable-select open-pseudo

title: Spinners from aria-busy
description: aria-busy=true is all it takes to show a spinner.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback aria-busy A spinner class for sighted users and `aria-busy` for assistive technology, kept in sync. `[aria-busy="true"]` is the only switch, and a `::before` ring spins. animations-css not

title: A switch from a checkbox
description: A native checkbox, appearance: none and an outline trick.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A `<button>` with `aria-checked` toggled in JavaScript, or a hidden checkbox plus extra spans. `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` with `appearance: none` draws its own track and dot. appearance light-dark

title: A header that knows it's stuck
description: scroll-state() container queries give a stuck table header and a scrolled dialog their shadows.
headings: The problem The trick Scroll shadows Try it Fallback scroll-state() A scroll listener, or an `IntersectionObserver` with a sentinel element. `container-type: scroll-state` and `@container scroll-state(stuck: block-start)` show the shadow. anchor-positioning container-scroll-state-queries

title: Tabs from radio buttons
description: Radio inputs, order and :nth-child(of S) for CSS-only tabs.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :nth-child(of S) JavaScript for clicks, `aria-selected` and panels, or CSS tabs with one selector per tab. One radio group, and `:checked + label + panel` shows the right panel. nth-child-of

title: Validation that waits with :user-invalid
description: :user-invalid shows errors after the user interacts, not on page load.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :user-invalid JavaScript that adds a touched class on blur. `:user-invalid` only matches after the user has changed the field. user-pseudos

title: Textareas that grow with field-sizing
description: field-sizing: content and lh units for auto-growing textareas.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback field-sizing JavaScript that resets the height to `scrollHeight` on every keystroke. `field-sizing: content` grows and shrinks the textarea with its text. field-sizing lh

title: Tooltips with interestfor
description: interestfor, calc-size() and @position-try for tooltips that stay on screen.
headings: The problem The trick Staying on screen Try it Fallback interestfor Event listeners, delays and a positioning library that measures and flips. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning keeps it on screen. anchor-positioning calc-size interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Under the hood
description: Every component, built one step at a time. Pick a step and the demo runs only the CSS up to it.

title: Vertical rhythm with round()
description: round() snaps line heights and font sizes to a rhythm step.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback round() A Sass function per font size, which breaks once sizes are fluid. `round(up, value, step)` snaps every line height to the grid at computed time. registered-custom-properties round-mod-rem

title: Accordion Actions API
description: Reference for Accordion Actions HTML component.
terms: .ui-actions A group of actions, such as buttons. .ui-align-start Alignment Alignment for the actions.

title: Accordion Summary API
description: Reference for Accordion Summary HTML component.
terms: summary The always visible header. The marker. Renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. .ui-marker

title: Accordion API
description: Reference for Accordion HTML component.
terms: details.ui-accordion Container element. The always visible header. summary The marker. In Astro, React, Svelte and Vue, `AccordionSummary` renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. summary .ui-marker The collapsible content. .ui-content A group of actions, such as buttons. .ui-actions [name] Group Groups accordions so only one of them can be open at a time. .ui-marker-animation-flip .ui-marker-animation-turn Marker animation How the marker animates when the accordion opens. `rotate` turns it upside down, `flip` mirrors it, and `turn` gives a chevron that points to the inline end a quarter turn, so it points down when open. [open] State Whether the accordion is open. .ui-elevated .ui-outlined .ui-tonal .ui-transparent Variants The variant to use. The default `plain` accordion has the page surface and no border, like a Card. `transparent` has no surface, border or padding.

title: Anchor API
description: Reference for Anchor HTML component.
terms: .ui-anchor Container element. Scopes the anchor to its content. The content the floating content is anchored to. .ui-anchor > :first-child The floating content. .ui-floating --ui-anchor-position-area Position Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the floating content is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the content's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page. [popover="hint"] Trigger Shows the floating content on hover and focus with `popover="hint"`. Without it, the content always shows.

title: Avatar Group API
description: Reference for Avatar Group HTML component.
terms: .ui-avatar-group A group of overlapping avatars.

title: Avatar API
description: Reference for Avatar HTML component.
terms: .ui-avatar Container element. The avatar image. img .ui-rounded .ui-squared .ui-squircle Shape The shape of the avatar. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the element. .ui-outlined .ui-tonal Variants The variant to use. `filled` is the primary color, `tonal` its tint and `outlined` the border color with no fill. button[disabled] a[aria-disabled="true"] State Disables a button avatar. A link avatar, which can't take `disabled`, drops its `href` and takes `aria-disabled="true"` instead.

title: Badge API
description: Reference for Badge HTML component.
terms: .ui-badge Container element. The element the badge is anchored to. .ui-badge > :first-child The indicator, inside `.ui-floating`. Holds `label`, the visible text with `hideLabel`, or only screen reader text with `dot`. .ui-indicator .ui-critical .ui-info .ui-neutral .ui-success .ui-warning Colors Optional colors. .ui-end-end .ui-end-start .ui-start-start Position The corner the indicator sits on. .ui-dot Dot Renders the indicator as a dot. `label` stays as screen reader text, and the `indicator` slot isn't shown. .ui-sr-only Label Hides `label` visually, for the whole sentence screen readers read, such as "5 unread messages". The `indicator` slot then holds the visible text and is hidden from screen readers. .ui-invisible Invisible Hides the indicator.

title: Button Group API
description: Reference for Button Group HTML component.
terms: .ui-button-group Container element. The buttons and button links. .ui-button-group > :first-child .ui-critical .ui-primary Colors Optional colors for the buttons. .ui-vertical Orientation The orientation of the element. .ui-overflow-scroll .ui-overflow-shrink Overflow What the items do when they don't fit. `"wrap"` wraps them onto more rows, `"scroll"` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `"shrink"` keeps them on one row and truncates labels with an ellipsis. Icon-only items keep their size. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the buttons. .ui-filled .ui-outlined .ui-tonal Variants The variant of the buttons.

title: Button API
description: Reference for Button HTML component.
terms: .ui-button Container element. An optional icon. .ui-button > svg An optional keyboard hint. .ui-button kbd .ui-critical .ui-primary Colors Optional colors. [aria-current="page"] [disabled] a[aria-disabled="true"] State Keeps the pressed background on a transparent (text) button link for the current page in navigation, or dims a disabled one. A link button, which can't take `disabled`, drops its `href` and takes `aria-disabled="true"` instead. .ui-round Shape Fully rounded corners, a circle when icon-only. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the element. .ui-filled .ui-outlined .ui-tonal Variants The variant to use.

title: Callout API
description: Reference for Callout HTML component.
terms: .ui-callout Container element. An optional icon before the content. In Astro, React, Svelte and Vue, `CalloutIcon` renders the default one for info, success, warning and critical. .ui-callout > svg The content, with an optional heading first. .ui-content .ui-critical .ui-info .ui-neutral .ui-success .ui-warning Severities The severity. Sets the color, and in Astro, React, Svelte and Vue the icon `CalloutIcon` renders. .ui-outlined Variants The variant to use.

title: Card Actions API
description: Reference for Card Actions HTML component.
terms: .ui-actions A group of actions, such as buttons. .ui-align-start Alignment Alignment for the actions.

title: Card API
description: Reference for Card HTML component.
terms: .ui-card Container element. The card header. hgroup.ui-header The card content. .ui-content A group of actions, such as buttons. .ui-actions .ui-dense .ui-spacious Density How much room the parts get. `spacious` pads them with `--ui-space-5` for a card that stands alone, such as a sign-in form, `dense` with `--ui-space-2` for a small stat. .ui-elevated .ui-outlined .ui-tonal .ui-transparent Variants The variant to use. The default `plain` card has the page surface color and no border.

title: Carousel API
description: Reference for Carousel HTML component.
terms: ul.ui-carousel The scroller. An item. .ui-carousel > :first-child The previous button. `::scroll-button(block-start)` when vertical. .ui-carousel::scroll-button(inline-start) The next button. `::scroll-button(block-end)` when vertical. .ui-carousel::scroll-button(inline-end) A marker, one per item. .ui-carousel > :first-child::scroll-marker .ui-align-center Alignment Where items snap. [aria-label] Label Accessible name of the carousel. --_media-aspect-ratio Aspect ratio Aspect ratio that images, videos and iframes are cropped to. .ui-buttons-none .ui-buttons-outside Buttons Previous and next buttons. `"outside"` places them beside the items, and `"none"` leaves them out. --_items-per-view Items per view Number of visible items. .ui-markers Markers One marker per item, after the list. .ui-vertical Orientation The orientation of the element. A vertical carousel is `--_block-size` tall, `24rem` by default. .ui-peek Peek Shows part of the neighboring items. .ui-persistent-buttons Persistent buttons Keeps the buttons visible at the ends. A disabled button has a muted border. .ui-stretch Stretch Makes each item a grid, so its content (a card, a link) fills the item's height. Media with an aspect ratio keeps it.

title: Checkbox Input API
description: Reference for Checkbox Input HTML component.
terms: input[type="checkbox"] The checkbox input, without a label. [data-indeterminate] State Shows a partially checked state. Sets the `indeterminate` property on the `<input>`.

title: Checkbox API
description: Reference for Checkbox HTML component.
terms: label.ui-checkbox Container element. The checkbox input. input The label. .ui-label Supporting text displayed below the label. .ui-end-text .ui-card Card Renders the checkbox as a card: a padded, outlined surface that tints when hovered and when checked, with the label and `endText` inside. Add `spread` to put the input at the end, and `variant` to change the surface. [aria-disabled="true"] [disabled] Disabled Dims the checkbox and shows a not-allowed cursor. `aria-disabled="true"` looks the same, but keeps the checkbox focusable and its value in the form, and doesn't stop the change, so block it with a script. [aria-invalid="true"] Validation Marks the control invalid and shows error styles. .ui-sr-only Label Visually hides the label, `.ui-sr-only` instead of `.ui-label`. [data-indeterminate] State Shows a partially checked state. Sets the `indeterminate` property on the `<input>`. .ui-vertical Orientation The orientation of the element. `vertical` stacks the label under the input. [required] Required Adds a required mark after the label. description: Reference for Textarea HTML component.
terms: label.ui-textarea Container element. The label for the field. .ui-label Start text displayed above the field. .ui-start-text The boxed textarea area. .ui-field Content above the textarea, inside the border, with a divider. .ui-field > .ui-top Content at the inline-start of the field, inside the border. .ui-field > .ui-start The textarea element. textarea Content at the inline-end of the field, inside the border. .ui-field > .ui-end Content below the textarea, inside the border, with a divider. .ui-field > .ui-bottom Supporting text displayed below the field. .ui-end-text The character count, `aria-hidden` so it stays out of the field's name. Near the limit, a live region outside the label announces the characters left. .ui-end-text > .ui-value .ui-auto-fit Auto fit Lets the width follow the content and allows resizing in both directions. [disabled] Disabled Dims the field and blocks input. [aria-invalid="true"] Validation Marks the control invalid and shows error styles. .ui-sr-only Label Visually hides the label, `.ui-sr-only` instead of `.ui-label`. The field keeps it as its accessible name. [required] Required Adds a required mark after the label. The form won't submit while the field is empty. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the element. .ui-spread Spread Pushes the label and start text to one side and the textarea to the other. .ui-filled Variants The variant to use.

title: Timeline Item API
description: Reference for Timeline Item HTML component.
terms: li An event. Replaces the dot with an icon. It follows the item's color and the current state. .ui-marker The date, in its own column. time The title of the event. h3 .ui-critical .ui-info .ui-neutral .ui-success .ui-warning Colors Optional colors. [aria-current] Current Marks the current item, which fills its marker with the primary color and a halo. `true` renders `aria-current="true"`, and `"step"`, `"date"` or `"time"` that value. [datetime] Datetime The machine-readable date of `time`.

title: Timeline API
description: Reference for Timeline HTML component.
terms: ol.ui-timeline Container element. An event, with its marker and the line to the next one. li .ui-small Sizes The size of the element. .ui-tracked Tracked Colors the line and the plain markers before the current item with the primary color, like a progress tracker.

title: Toast API
description: Reference for Toast HTML component.
terms: opui-toaster.ui-toaster The `<opui-toaster>` custom element, with `display: contents`. A button with `commandfor` and `command="--toast"` shows a toast with its `data-toast` text and `data-toast-severity`, and `toast(message, { action, duration, severity })` or `toast.success(message)` does it from a script, where `action` takes a `label` and an `onClick`. `dismiss(toast)` returns a promise that resolves once the toast is gone. The stack of toasts, a manual popover at the block end and the inline end of the viewport unless `side` and `align` move it. It opens with the first toast and closes after the last. ol A toast, a `Callout` with the severity class, its icon, the message in `.ui-content`, an action `Button` when it has an `action`, and a close `Button`. The element adds it, and on dismiss makes it `inert`, fades it out and closes its gap before it removes it. ol > .ui-callout The live region that announces each toast, visually hidden with `.ui-sr-only` and outside the popover, so it's always in the page. [role="status"] .ui-align-center .ui-align-start Alignment Where the toasts sit along their side of the viewport. [close-label] Label The accessible name of the close button of each toast. [duration] Duration How long a toast stays, in milliseconds, while the pointer and focus are elsewhere. .ui-block-start Position The side of the viewport the toasts sit on.

title: Toggle Button API
description: Reference for Toggle Button HTML component.
terms: label.ui-toggle-button Container element. A visually hidden checkbox or radio input. .ui-toggle-button > input [checked] Checked Selects the button. [disabled] Disabled Disables the button. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the element. [type="checkbox"] [type="radio"] Type The input type. `"radio"` allows one selection in a group. A `ToggleGroup` without `multiple` makes every button a radio.

title: Toggle Group API
description: Reference for Toggle Group HTML component.
terms: .ui-toggle-group Container element. A toggle button. .ui-toggle-group > .ui-toggle-button:first-child [role="group"] Multiple Lets several buttons be checked, with checkbox inputs. Without it, one button is checked at a time, with radio inputs in a `[role="radiogroup"]`. .ui-vertical Orientation The orientation of the element. .ui-overflow-scroll .ui-overflow-shrink Overflow What the items do when they don't fit. `"wrap"` wraps them onto more rows, `"scroll"` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `"shrink"` keeps them on one row and truncates labels with an ellipsis. Icon-only items keep their size. .ui-large .ui-small .ui-x-small Sizes The size of the buttons.

title: Tooltip API
description: Reference for Tooltip HTML component.
terms: .ui-tooltip Container element. The trigger that shows the tooltip on hover and focus. .ui-tooltip > :first-child The tooltip, a `popover="hint"`. .ui-floating .ui-arrow Arrow Adds an arrow that points to the trigger. --ui-anchor-position-area Position Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the tooltip is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the tooltip's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page.

title: Typography API
description: Reference for Typography HTML component.
terms: .ui-rich-text Classless typography for uncontrolled child markup. .ui-blockquote Blockquote Quoted block with a start border. .ui-caption Caption Muted supporting text. pre.ui-code-block Code block Monospace preformatted block. .ui-critical .ui-info .ui-neutral .ui-success .ui-warning Colors Tone of `.ui-swatch`, and the text color of `.ui-p`, `.ui-caption` and `.ui-overline`. Without it, the swatch takes the palette accent of the scope it sits in. .ui-h1 .ui-h2 .ui-h3 .ui-h4 .ui-h5 .ui-h6 Heading Heading styles for any element. .ui-hgroup Heading group Groups an overline, heading, and optional body copy. .ui-icon Icon Sizes an inline `svg` to `--ui-icon-size` and keeps it from shrinking in a flex row. .ui-abbr .ui-cite .ui-del .ui-dfn .ui-ins .ui-kbd .ui-mark .ui-s .ui-samp .ui-small .ui-sub .ui-sup .ui-u .ui-var Inline Inline text element utilities. .ui-link Link Link styles outside `.ui-rich-text`. On hover and focus, the underline gets thicker. The color gets darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode. .ui-not-rich-text Not rich text Ends the `.ui-rich-text` styles inside it. .ui-overline Overline Small uppercase label text. .ui-p Paragraph Body paragraph styling. .ui-large .ui-small Sizes Size modifiers on `.ui-p` and `.ui-icon`. An icon reads `--ui-icon-size-small` and `--ui-icon-size-large`. .ui-tabular-nums Tabular nums Digits of one width, so numbers line up in a column of prices or stats. .ui-swatch Swatch A small colored dot for a legend, in `--_swatch-bg-color`, the palette accent of its tone or scope.
